subject: Proposed MSA changes re: termination for convenience and auto-renew mechanics
messages:
From: Lara Diaz <contract.manager@evergreen.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MSA changes re: TFC and auto-renew — Evergreen request

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal at Evergreen reviewed the draft MSA + order form and we have two related asks we'd like Redwood to consider before we can move to signature:

1) Termination for Convenience (TFC): Evergreen cannot accept an uncapped unilateral TFC. We need either (a) no TFC, or (b) mutual TFC limited by a termination fee that scales with remaining committed spend.

2) Auto-renew and notice windows: We need clearer timing — procurement requires a 90 day notice to opt-out of auto-renew for the production environment. For pilots we can accept a shorter window but need to ensure the order form flags which seats are pilot vs prod.

Attached are our redlines (Evergreen_MSA_redlines.docx) and the current order form (OrderForm_v2.pdf). Can your team propose concrete language that reconciles our risk posture with Redwood's need for predictable commitments? Ideally we get a revised order form + summary by end of week so procurement can approve.

Thanks,
Lara Diaz
Sr. Contracts Manager | Evergreen Health
procurement@evergreen.health

Attachments: Evergreen_MSA_redlines.docx (docx), OrderForm_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Lara Diaz <contract.manager@evergreen.health>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA changes re: TFC and auto-renew — Redwood response

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear redlines. Appreciate the quick read from Evergreen Legal/Procurement.

High-level reaction and two compromise paths we can propose to our legal team:

Option A (Customer-favorable): Remove unilateral TFC; replace with mutual TFC only. Auto-renew remains but with a 120-day notice for production environments and 30-day notice for pilots. Redwood would accept a termination fee equal to 2 months' average spend (cap) if Evergreen exercises TFC within the first 12 months.

Option B (Redwood-favorable): Retain unilateral TFC but with a 60-day notice plus a graduated termination fee based on remaining committed months (month-percentage). Auto-renew notice stays at 90 days for production.

Next steps: I'll loop in Naomi and Ben for legal redlines and risk/finance impact. We'll turn around a redlined OrderForm_v3 and a short summary showing the cost/commitment tradeoffs. Can you confirm Evergreen's preference between Option A or B so we prioritize?

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

Attachment: OrderForm_v3-redline.pdf (pdf)

On Wed, Jun 24, 2026 at 09:12 AM Lara Diaz <contract.manager@evergreen.health> wrote:
> Hi Michael,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA changes re: TFC and auto-renew — legal POV and compromise language

Michael / Ben —

Reviewed Lara's redlines. My suggested approach to reduce legal friction while protecting Redwood economics:

1) Mutual TFC with scaled termination fee (preferred compromise):
  - Mutual TFC allowed after initial 90-day non-cancellable period.
  - Termination fee = remaining committed monthly average * 0.5 for months 1–6, 0.25 for months 7–12, waived after month 12. Cap the fee at 3 months' average spend.

2) Auto-renew windows and notice:
  - Production SKUs: auto-renew 12-month terms, opt-out notice = 120 days prior to renewal date.
  - Pilot SKUs: auto-renew on 30-day notice, pilot flag must be set on the order form.

3) Order form amendment fields: add explicit start/end dates per SKU, call out pilot vs prod, and a line for "Termination fee calculation" to avoid later procurement disputes.

4) Rollout / operational fallback: if customer elects TFC and we cannot meet SLA during the runout period, include a service continuity carveout and a limited transition support fee.

I'll draft precise MSA language and an OrderForm amendment. Michael—if Evergreen is open to the scaled-fee approach, we can present that as Option A (mutual TFC, scaled fee). If they insist on no TFC, that's likely a price/commitment conversation with finance.

Linking HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345678 (RDW-3459)

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA changes re: TFC and auto-renew — exec guidance

Team — quick exec guidance so Legal has clear constraints before drafting final language:

- We should avoid an uncapped unilateral TFC; mutual TFC with a scaled fee is acceptable. Finance wants a cap at 3 months' average spend.
- Keep production opt-out at 120 days. Procurement concessions for pilots OK at 30 days, but require clear pilot designation in the order form and a max pilot duration (90 days).
- If we add a termination fee schedule, include an explicit waiver trigger (e.g., change in law or force majeure) to avoid reflexive disputes.
- Ask: Naomi, please produce a redline MSA paragraph and a short one-page memo explaining the customer impact (price/exposure) so Sales can present to Evergreen's VP Procurement. We need that memo by EOD Friday.

Marissa
VP, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Lara Diaz <contract.manager@evergreen.health>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MSA changes re: TFC and auto-renew — Evergreen confirmation

Michael / Naomi / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick iterations and the clear options. Evergreen can accept the mutual TFC approach with the following explicit terms:

- Mutual TFC allowed after an initial 90-day non-cancellable period.
- Termination fee: remaining committed monthly average * 0.5 for months 1–6, 0.25 for months 7–12, waived afterward. Cap at 2 months' average spend (we counter-propose cap change to 2 months).
- Production auto-renew opt-out notice: 120 days (agreed).
- Pilot opt-out: 30 days, pilot flag on the order form and pilot duration capped at 90 days.

We can sign-off on a redlined OrderForm_v3 that mirrors these points and a short memo of impact from Redwood. Once we have the redlines, Evergreen will route to VP Procurement for final sign-off.

Please send an updated OrderForm_v3 and the one-page memo to procurement@evergreen.health.

Best,
Lara Diaz
Sr. Contracts Manager | Evergreen Health
contract.manager@evergreen.health

Attachments referenced earlier: OrderForm_v2.pdf, Evergreen_MSA_redlines.docx
